overall: On reconsideration, the AG kept the finding that the committee violated the law by not reviewing the January 25 complaint, but found it was not intentional, found no violation on the February 15 complaint, withdrew the hearing referral, and closed the matter.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to list an anticipated executive session discussion on a meeting notice with enough detail.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we find that the Committee listed the anticipated executive session topic with sufficient specificity on a meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee did not respond to a request for executive session minutes within the time required by law.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee's failure to conduct this review within the required time frame violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee did not conduct periodic reviews of its executive session minutes to justify continued nondisclosure.
allegations.key_passage: This failure to review executive session minutes violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to meet to review the first Open Meeting Law complaint before responding to it (reconsidered: violation affirmed, not intentional).
allegations.key_passage: While we affirm our finding that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law, in light of these facts we find that the failure to review the January 25 complaint was not an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to meet to review the second Open Meeting Law complaint before the chair responded (reconsidered: no violation).
allegations.key_passage: Based on these facts, we find that the Committee complied with its obligations with respect to the February 15 complaint.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked the AG to review all agendas, minutes and notices for compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Our office does not generally conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations and decline to do so here.

remedy: Recommended a $1,000 fine and an order of immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (original July 21 determination; the hearing referral was withdrawn on reconsideration and the matter closed).
remedy_passage: We recommend a fine of $1,000 and an order of immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
